name: HIMARS (M142)
representative_system: M142 HIMARS, firing GMLRS / ER GMLRS / ATACMS

cost.display: ~$3.5–5.3M per launcher (rising over production lots); a single GMLRS rocket runs ~$170K, ER GMLRS ~$434K, and an ATACMS missile over $1M

key_facts.label: Reach
key_facts.value: ~70 km (ER GMLRS); ATACMS variants to ~300 km

key_facts.label: Reload
key_facts.value: Self-loads a fresh 6-rocket pod in minutes

short_role: Wheeled, truck-mounted rocket artillery used for deep, precision strikes on command posts, logistics and ammunition depots well behind the immediate line.
characteristics: Fires GMLRS-family guided rockets (~70 km with ER GMLRS) or ATACMS ballistic missiles (up to ~300 km)
GPS/INS-guided rounds land within a few meters, unlike unguided tube artillery at that range
High road speed and a short reload cycle support the same 'shoot and scoot' discipline as towed artillery
Compatible with the next-generation Precision Strike Missile, extending reach beyond 500 km
employment_notes: Used deliberately, not continuously — each launch is expensive enough that targets are pre-vetted against ISR (drone and satellite imagery) rather than fired reactively the way a howitzer answers a call for fire. It has been used against ammunition depots, command posts and bridges at depths conventional tube artillery cannot reach.
contrast_vs_traditional: Traditional deep-strike capability belonged almost exclusively to air power. A truck-mounted rocket system that a small crew can hide, move and fire from the operational-near band gives a much smaller force the ability to hold operational-depth targets at risk — but at a cost per shot high enough that, unlike the FPV drones flooding the front, every launch is a deliberate, ISR-cued decision rather than a routine one.

reactive_behavior.description: On select: launcher elevates, fires a rocket pod, brief downrange flight and impact marker.

connections.description: Commercial satellite imagery used to vet high-value targets before committing a launch.
